holidays.name: National Comic Book Day
holidays.description: A day for fans to dust off their longboxes, binge on superhero sagas, and celebrate the art of sequential storytelling, from caped crusaders to indie weirdos.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that grew out of comic fan communities and retailers, who wanted a day to honor the medium and its creators.
holidays.funFact: Action Comics #1, featuring the debut of Superman, has sold for millions of dollars, making it one of the most valuable comic books ever.

holidays.name: National Lobster Thermidor Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the fancy French dish of lobster meat cooked in a rich creamy sauce of egg yolks, brandy, and mustard, stuffed back into the shell and browned under the broiler.
holidays.origin: A food-calendar observance honoring the classic French recipe, which is said to have been created in Paris in 1894 and named after the play Thermidor.
holidays.funFact: The dish is reportedly named after the play Thermidor by Victorien Sardou, which premiered the same year the restaurant Maire is said to have first served it.

holidays.name: World Pharmacists Day
holidays.description: A global day when people thank the folks behind the counter who decode doctors' handwriting and keep medicine safe and understandable.
holidays.origin: Established by the International Pharmaceutical Federation (FIP) in 2009 and held on September 25, the anniversary of the organization's founding in 1912.
holidays.funFact: The FIP chose September 25 because the federation was founded on that date in 1912 in The Hague.

holidays.name: National One-Hit Wonder Day
holidays.description: A day to blast that one song you can sing every word of, but cannot name a second hit by the same artist. Expect lots of karaoke and nostalgic playlists.
holidays.origin: An unofficial pop culture observance created by music fans and radio stations to celebrate artists who struck lightning once.
holidays.funFact: Many one-hit wonders are not truly one-hit; artists like Right Said Fred and Soft Cell had other chart success in other countries, but are remembered for a single US smash.

holidays.name: National Crush a Can Day
holidays.description: A noisy observance encouraging people to flatten their empty aluminum cans and recycle them, with extra points for dramatic stomping.
holidays.origin: A recycling-awareness observance promoted by environmental groups and waste management advocates to encourage tidy recycling habits.
holidays.funFact: Aluminum cans can be recycled and back on store shelves in as little as 60 days, and recycling aluminum saves about 95 percent of the energy needed to make new aluminum.
